name: Thrashing: E = r kills A = r, backtracking redoes B, C, D
note: Order A, B, C, D, E. E has the single value r, so A = r can never work, but plain backtracking only finds out at the very end: it first assigns all six permutations of x, y, z to B, C, D (they must differ) and fails at E each time. Run Backtracking: 45 values tried ('most constraints first' needs only 10). Run Forward checking: A = r empties D(E) at once, 6 values tried. Run Conflict-directed backjumping: 16, because it jumps from E straight to A. Watch the nodes counter.
